8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57

63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end
188	
189	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/
75	
76	set_option autoImplicit false
77	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

81	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
82	
83	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
84	
85	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

89	noncomputable section
90	
91	variable (C) in
92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/
99	def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
103	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s
104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
116	that is not needed. -/
117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl
121	
122	/-! ## The coupling -/
123	
124	variable (C) in
125	/-- **THE COUPLING**: pointwise coverage for `f` plus a range containment gives pointwise
126	coverage for the restricted family.
127	
128	The containment is the honest content: at the point, index and witness coverage produces, the
129	witness's image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the
130	open immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`, which is `rfl` — so this direction
131	carries no mathematics beyond the lift, and together with its converse below it is a
132	biconditional rather than a reduction.  **It closes no gate.**
133	
134	Note the shape of the hypothesis: it quantifies over the data coverage *returns*, not over all
135	opens or all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness,
136	which is the only place the information is available; a formulation asking for the containment
137	uniformly over all witnesses would be strictly stronger.
138	
139	What the containment *means* geometrically depends on which open `V i` is, and this file
140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source
141	while `chartLocus` is a set on a test, so the two are not interchangeable and the intended
142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
145	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
146	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
149	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx
155	
156	variable (C) in
157	/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.
161	
162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/
179	
180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183	
184	So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
185	is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
186	restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
187	its classes inside `V i`.
188	
189	The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by
191	`restrictChart_app_apply`. -/
192	theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
193	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
194	    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
195	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
196	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
197	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
198	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
199	  intro T s t
200	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
201	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
202	  intro z hz
203	  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
204	  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩
205	
206	end
207	
208	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
12	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
13	`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
14	problem this file addresses.
15	
16	**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
17	`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
18	systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
19	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
20	comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
21	test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
22	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
23	(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
24	lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
25	use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.
26	
27	It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.
28	
29	## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
30	
31	The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
32	as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
33	the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
34	and each is where the argument could fail:
35	
36	* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
37	  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
38	  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
39	  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
40	  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
41	* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
42	  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
43	  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
44	  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
45	  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
46	* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
47	  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
48	  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.
49	
50	None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
51	affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
52	geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.
53	
54	## What this does and does not buy
55	
56	It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
57	asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
58	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
59	with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
60	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
61	of the ring-indexed machinery directly.
62	
63	It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
64	open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
65	the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
66	a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
67	tree's producers live.
68	
69	**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
70	`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited
71	that as discharging the `reduction-needs-its-converse` safeguard.  It does not: that
72	declaration is `rfl`-equal to `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally`, its `[IsAffine Y]` binder is
73	never used, and the direction it certifies is the *free* one — general pointwise data gives the
74	affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
75	general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
76	honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is
77	kept only as the affine-test instance of the pointwise extraction, which is what it is.
78	
79	**On the atlas, and this is the sharper limit.**  Nothing here pins `V`.  The statements below
80	take an arbitrary family `f`, which is what makes the site content reusable — but a consumer
81	must supply coverage at the *same* `V` at which antecedent 1 was certified, and `ajcr-p1`
82	measured both ends of that range to be bad: `hf` is free at `V = ⊥` (`isChartUniv_bot`, with a
83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
87	check.
88	
89	## Main declarations
90	
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine` — **the site fact**, with no
92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.
97	  the instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test data alone.
98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the converse, so the affine form
99	  is not a strengthening.
100	-/
101	
102	set_option autoImplicit false
103	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
104	
105	universe u
106	
107	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
108	
109	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
110	
111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
112	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
113	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
114	
115	noncomputable section
116	
117	/-! ## The site fact -/
118	
119	/-- **A sieve is covering as soon as it is covering after pullback to affine pieces.**
120	
121	Stated for an arbitrary sieve on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses.  The
122	cover is `Scheme.affineCover`, whose members are affine by
123	`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`, and the deduction is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`
124	against the presieve the cover generates.
125	
126	This is the step the coverage chain was missing: it says the Zariski-local-surjectivity
127	obligation may be discharged one affine piece of the test at a time. -/
128	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
129	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
130	      Scheme.zariskiTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
131	    S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
132	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
133	      ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T :=
134	    Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
135	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
136	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
137	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
138	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
139	
140	/-! ## The reduction -/
141	
142	variable (C) in
143	/-- **THE AFFINE-TEST REDUCTION**: pointwise coverage over affine tests gives
144	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
145	
146	The hypothesis is `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`'s, with `[IsAffine Y]` added and
147	nothing else changed.  So a coverage producer may assume its test is affine — hence, through
148	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, that its divisor data lives over a *ring*, which is where every
149	producer in this project is stated. -/
150	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
151	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
156	  intro T s
157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)
163	          ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s) := by
164	    -- `Sieve.pullback` preserves `iSup` (it is a left adjoint), and per index it turns the
165	    -- image sieve of `s` into that of `s` restricted along the cover map
166	    simp only [← Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
167	    ext Y g
168	    simp only [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply, Sieve.pullback_apply]
169	    aesop
170	  rw [hpb]
171	  -- the piece is affine (`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`), so the hypothesis applies AT IT — note
172	  -- `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` cannot be cited here, since it quantifies over all tests
173	  -- and would demand the datum at the non-affine ones too; the site bridge is what is reused
174	  choose W hW i x hx using h (T.affineCover.X j)
175	    ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s)
176	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun y => ⟨x y, hx y⟩
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **B-5 over affine tests ⟹ B-6**: the local-surjectivity instance
180	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test coverage data alone. -/
181	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
182	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
183	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
184	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
185	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
186	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
187	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C f h)
188	
189	/-! ## The converse -/
190	
191	variable (C) in
192	/-- **The affine form is not a strengthening**: `ChartsCoverLocally` gives back, over each
193	affine test, a cover on whose members some chart hits the section.
194	
195	Read the carrier honestly, exactly as `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` does: the sieve
196	condition returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with open-immersion maps, not by opens of
197	the test, so the converse produces a cover map where the hypothesis consumed an opens
198	inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — that the affine-only hypothesis is available, not
199	chosen for provability — a cover map is exactly as good. -/
200	theorem affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
201	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
202	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
203	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) :
204	    ∃ (𝒰 : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
205	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
206	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s :=
207	  pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s
208	
209	end
210	
211	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageFibre
7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 assembly: from the fibre step to `chartLocus` membership over a GENERAL test
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
12	produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
13	(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:
14	
15	```
16	∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
17	```
18	
19	This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:
20	
21	* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
22	  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;
23	* `chartLocus` is *defined* as the split-witness predicate of the twisted class at that field
24	  point, and the twist commutes with restriction (`picEtMap_chartTwist`), so
25	  "`IsSplitWitness` of the twisted fibre class" **is** membership, by `Iff.rfl`.
26	
27	The second point is worth stating as a lemma rather than inlining: `chartTwist` is applied to
28	`lam` over `T` and then restricted, whereas the fibre step produces the twist of the
29	*restricted* class over `κ(t)`.  Those are equal, but not syntactically — `picEtMap_chartTwist`
30	is the law, and `mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` is the resulting membership rule.
31	
32	## What remains of B-5 after this file
33	
34	**Twice corrected; read the DEFECT section for the full history.**  This header first said the
35	only residues were the two per-fibre choices; a degree probe added a third (step 6's feedback);
36	and on 2026-07-28 that third was **removed again** — not by discharging it but by showing
37	coverage needs no drop, hence no feedback (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  Step 2 is
38	likewise landed now (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`).
39	
40	The two per-fibre choices, which are residues *of the route through this file*:
41	
42	* **step 3, the twist exponent `m`.**  Chosen against the fibre's OWN DAT-0a bound `b_L`.  No
43	  uniform `m₀` exists (§0.2.2, I-0204), so this is a genuine `∃ m` produced inside the
44	  coverage proof, at the fibre.
45	* **step 5's oracle instantiation.**  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at
46	  `P :=` the base-changed `K_s`-points, whose `residueDeg = 1` comes from
47	  `rationalPointBaseChange_snd`.
48	
49	Both are `L`-level statements; neither is `divRep`- or certificate-gated.  Everything between
50	them and `chartLocus` membership is now landed.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` — the membership rule: a split
55	  witness for the twisted *fibre* class puts `t` in `chartLocus`.
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_drop` — **the B-5 assembly**: the fibre step's
57	  hypotheses, at `K := κ(t)`, give `t ∈ chartLocus`.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
62	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
63	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
64	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
65	
66	universe u
67	
68	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
69	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
70	
71	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
72	
73	open AlgebraicJacobian
74	
75	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
76	
77	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
78	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
79	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
80	
81	noncomputable section
82	
83	/-! ## The membership rule -/
84	
85	variable (C) in
86	/-- **A split witness for the twisted FIBRE class puts the point in `chartLocus`.**
87	
88	`chartLocus` twists over `T` and then restricts to `κ(t)`; the fibre step produces the twist of
89	the already-restricted class.  `picEtMap_chartTwist` says those agree, and
90	`chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass` puts both in the collapsed spelling the fibre
91	step uses.
92	
93	Stated as a named rule because the two sides differ syntactically and a lane that inlines the
94	substitution will meet the mismatch inside a proof about degrees, where it is least welcome. -/
95	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre (m : ℕ)
96	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
97	    (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
98	    (h : IsSplitWitness C
99	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam
100	        * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k (Over.testPointField t)))) :
101	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
102	  rw [mem_chartLocus_iff, picEtMap_chartTwist,
103	    chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass]
104	  exact h
105	
106	/-! ## A DEFECT IN THIS FILE'S OWN COMPOSITION CLAIM — read before using `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`
107	
108	Found by a degree probe on this file, the same session it was written, and stated here rather
109	than quietly repaired because the theorems below are **true and correctly proved** — what was
110	wrong is the account of how they compose.
111	
112	**The arithmetic.** `hW₀` puts `W₀` in the class `M₀ · (twist class at Z)`.  For a degree-zero
113	`λ` the presenting class `M₀` has `classDeg = 0`, so
114	
115	  `deg W₀ = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,
116	
117	and `hdeg` demands `deg W₀ = g + e`.  Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g`
118	those force **`e = 0`**: the drop budget is zero and the greedy drop does nothing.  (Verified by
119	deriving `(e : ℤ) = 0` from exactly this hypothesis pack.)
120	
121	**What that means.** The pack is *satisfiable* — it instantiates, and at `e = 0` the theorem is
122	the true statement "a witness of degree `g` gives `chartLocus` membership".  It is not vacuous.
123	But `w4-datb` §1.2's argument runs the drop at a **different stage** from the chart index:
124	
125	* the drop runs on `λ·θᵐ` — i.e. at `Z := 0`, where `chartTwistClass C m 0 = θᵐ` and the degree
126	  is `m·d₁`, so the budget is `e = m·d₁ − g`, nonzero for the `m` step 3 chooses;
127	* its **output** `Σ` is then the chart index's `Z`, at which the twisted class has degree `g`.
128	
129	So one `Z` is an input and the other is an output, and this file's headline claim that "steps
130	4–6 are discharged" conflated them.  Steps 4 and 5 (the vanishing witness and the drop) are
131	discharged **at `Z := 0`** by `exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop`; step 6 — feeding `Σ` back as the
132	index and re-reading membership at the *new* `Z` — is **NOT** discharged, and needs the
133	graph-class transport of `Picard/Pic0ChartRationalGraph.lean` applied to the drop's output.
134	
135	**Corrected status of B-5, 2026-07-28 — and the correction is a REMOVAL of both residues this
136	section named.**  The arithmetic above is right and the two-stage reading of `w4-datb` §1.2 is
137	right; what was wrong is treating the drop as *necessary*.
138	
139	* the step-6 feedback is not a residue: coverage needs no drop at all, because
140	  `IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` alone (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  With the
141	  drop gone there is one `Z` and nothing to feed back;
142	* step 2 is landed (`PicEtAff.degAff_map` → `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`).
143	
144	What remains of B-5 is step 3's per-fibre `m`.
145	
146	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This said "and even that is now *derived* rather than chosen:
147	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` takes the DAT-0a threshold `b_L` in the shape
148	`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` produces it, so instantiating DAT-0a at
149	the base-changed curve is the whole remaining work."  FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter
150	`n` that theorem's `hdeg` **forces** the threshold to equal `n` (`ledger_forces_b_eq_n`), and at
151	`n = g` the resulting hypothesis says every degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`
152	(`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`) — false on a curve with a moving degree-`g` family, and strictly above
153	DAT-0a's own bound `n₁·deg F + g`.  See `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`; the residue is
154	reconciling the chart parameter with the threshold, not instantiating DAT-0a.
155	
156	`mem_chartLocus_of_drop` stays sound and is still the right theorem when the `h⁰ = 1`
157	normalisation is wanted (DAT-C / GAP-2 need it; membership does not); use it knowing its `Z` is
158	the drop's input stage. -/
159	
160	/-! ## The assembly -/
161	
162	variable (C) in
163	/-- **THE B-5 ASSEMBLY** (`w4-datb` §1.2, everything except the two per-fibre choices).
164	
165	For a point `t` of a general test `T` and a plus class `lam` over `T`: given a finite separable
166	`L/κ(t)` presenting the fibre class, and a divisor `W₀` in the twisted class over `L` of degree
167	`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, the point `t` lies in `chartLocus C m Z lam` — and the drop at `L`
168	additionally yields the `h⁰ = 1` normalisation.
169	
170	**Reading this against `w4-datb` §1.2 — corrected, and the earlier version of this paragraph
171	was wrong in two places** (issues I-0614, I-0615).  It said "steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 are all
172	discharged".  Three of those five are; the other two are not:
173	
174	* **step 1 — discharged.**  The `hM₀` hypothesis, which `exists_splitting_of_picEt` supplies
175	  unconditionally.
176	* **step 2 — DISCHARGED 2026-07-28, this line supersedes the "NOT discharged" it replaced.**
177	  The missing input was base-field invariance of `degAff` under `PicEtAff.map`; it is now
178	  `PicEtAff.degAff_map` (`Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean`) and holds for an **arbitrary** field
179	  extension `L/K`, with no finiteness or separability.  Step 2 itself is
180	  `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero` (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`), and the whole
181	  twisted ledger closes to `g + e` there.
182	* **step 4 — discharged** as an input: `hdeg` + `h1`.
183	* **step 5 — discharged** by the oracle.
184	* **step 6 — NOT NEEDED, which supersedes "NOT discharged".**  The feedback is real for the
185	  route *through the drop*, and the DEFECT section's arithmetic stands.  But coverage does not
186	  need the drop: `IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` and for **neither** effectivity **nor**
187	  degree `g`, so a witness of the twisted class suffices and there is only ever one `Z`.  See
188	  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`, whose `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` strictly
189	  generalises this theorem's membership half — with `g`, `e`, `hχ`, `hdeg` and the whole oracle
190	  deleted rather than discharged.
191	* **step 3 — the residue this paragraph originally named**, and still a residue: `m`, `W₀` and
192	  `hdeg` are *inputs*, because `b_L` is per-fibre and does not transport (I-0204), so no
193	  formulation of this theorem can produce `m` for the caller.
194	
195	**Note one conclusion this theorem deliberately drops** — wanted not by coverage (which needs no
196	drop at all, see the step-6 entry above) but by DAT-C's canonical section and GAP-2 uniqueness:
197	the fibre step returns `S`'s support clause (`coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P`), and the `-` pattern below
198	discards it.  A lane closing step 6 should re-expose it — it is what says `Σ` is supported in
199	the rational points whose graph classes the index is built from. -/
200	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_drop {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
201	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
202	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
203	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
204	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L] [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
205	    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
206	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
207	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
208	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
209	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
210	    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
211	    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
212	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
213	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
214	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
215	    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
216	    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
217	      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
218	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
219	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
220	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
221	      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
222	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
223	        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
224	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
225	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
226	  obtain ⟨hsplit, S, hS0, hSdeg, -, hSh0, hSh1⟩ :=
227	    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam) m Z g e hχ M₀ hM₀
228	      W₀ hW₀ hdeg h1 P hdense hPcl hPdeg
229	  exact ⟨mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre C m Z lam t hsplit,
230	    S, hS0, hSdeg, hSh0, hSh1⟩
231

9	/-!
10	# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6
11	
12	A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
15	`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
16	**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
17	that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
18	open residues.
19	
20	**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**
21	
22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
23	
24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
28	*membership of the locus* needs.
29	
30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
35	the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.
36	
37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.
39	
40	## What coverage then needs, in full
41	
42	Exactly one input beyond the landed splitting: a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the
43	splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely
44	per-fibre (I-0204, `w4-datb` §0.2.2): no uniform `m₀` exists, so the exponent `m` must be chosen
45	against `L`'s own threshold `b_L`.
46	
47	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This paragraph continued: `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
48	"takes `b_L` in exactly the shape `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`
49	produces it, and *derives* the `m` — so what remains of step 3 is instantiating DAT-0a at the
50	base-changed curve, not choosing anything."  That is FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter
51	`n` the `hdeg` hypothesis **forces `b = n`**, and at `n = g` the resulting `hb` is a statement
52	that is false in general — see the retraction note on
53	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` itself and `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` for the
54	three machine-checked statements that replace it.  The theorem below is sound; only this account
55	of what remains was wrong.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` — **coverage, drop-free**: a splitting plus a
60	  vanishing witness in the twisted class gives `t ∈ chartLocus`.  No `g`, no `e`, no `χ`, no
61	  oracle, no effectivity.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the same with the witness *produced*
63	  from a degree threshold at the splitting field.  Sound; but read its retraction note before
64	  reading the threshold as DAT-0a's (it is forced to equal the chart parameter, I-0660).
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the `∃ m` form: the coverage
66	  statement `w4-datb` §1.2 targets, at a fixed chart-index shape.
67	-/

154	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
155	    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

240	      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
241	    ∃ m' : ℕ, ∃ Z' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, t ∈ chartLocus C m' Z' lam :=

10	/-!
11	# B-5, the fibre step: the greedy drop RUN at the splitting field, as a `chartLocus` witness
12	
13	**Title corrected (issue I-0615): this file is steps 4 and 5, not "4–6".**  Step 6 — feeding the
14	drop's output `Σ` back as the chart index — is NOT here and is not discharged anywhere; see the
15	DEFECT section of `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`, which explains why the drop stage and the
16	index stage carry different `Z`.  The original "4–6" wording is what that retraction corrects.
17	
18	`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5 happen entirely on the curve over the splitting field `L`.  This file
19	runs them and hands the result to `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`'s introduction rule, so
20	that what comes out is membership of `chartLocus`.
21	
22	## The statement, and what is a hypothesis rather than a construction
23	
24	`exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` takes:
25	
26	* the presentation of the *twisted* fibre class over `L` by a Čech class `M`
27	  (`hM` — supplied at step 1 by `picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit`);
28	* a divisor `W₀` in that class with vanishing `H¹` and degree `g + e`
29	  (`hdeg`/`h1` — supplied at step 4: the class's degree is computed by
30	  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean`, and the vanishing comes from the fibre's OWN
31	  vanishing bound, which is where step 3's per-fibre `m` is spent);
32	* the admissible point oracle at `L` (`hdense`/`hPcl`/`hPdeg` — supplied at step 5 by
33	  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at the base-changed `K_s`-points).
34	
35	and produces an `S ≥ 0` of degree `e`, supported in the oracle, with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`,
36	`h¹ = 0`, together with `IsSplitWitness` at the twisted class.
37	
38	**What is deliberately a hypothesis:** the *existence* of `W₀` of the right degree with
39	`h¹ = 0`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and per `w4-datb` §0.2.2 (the I-0204 discipline)
40	its bound `b_L` is a **per-fibre** constant that provably does not transport from `k` — so it
41	must be chosen at `L`, inside the coverage proof, against `L`'s own instance.  Threading it as
42	a hypothesis here keeps that choice visible instead of burying it: a caller who cannot produce
43	`W₀` has not yet done step 3.
44	
45	**Why the `h⁰ = 1` conclusion is carried even though `IsSplitWitness` does not ask for it:**
46	the witness predicate asks only for vanishing `H¹` (documented at `IsSplitWitness`; the
47	worksheets' "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`" is stronger than what the tree's
48	predicates state).  But `h⁰ = 1` is what DAT-C's normalization and GAP-2's uniqueness need, and
49	it is free here — the drop produces it.  Dropping it from the conclusion would force a later
50	lane to re-run the induction.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` — **the fibre step of B-5**: the greedy drop
55	  at `L`, packaged as `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class plus the `h⁰ = 1` normalization.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
60	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
61	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
62	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

66	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
67	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	open AlgebraicJacobian
72	
73	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
74	
75	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
76	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
77	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
78	
79	noncomputable section
80	
81	/-! ## The fibre step -/
82	
83	variable (C) in
84	/-- **B-5's fibre step** (`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5, run at the splitting field; **not** step 6 —
85	see the header correction and issue I-0615).
86	
87	Given the twisted fibre class presented over `L` by `M`, a divisor `W₀` in `M` of degree
88	`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, and an admissible point oracle `P` on the `L`-curve, the greedy
89	drop produces `S` of degree `e` supported in `P` with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1` and `h¹(W₀ − S) = 0`;
90	and the class of `W₀` itself already certifies `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class.
91	
92	The two conclusions serve different consumers, which is why both are returned: the
93	`IsSplitWitness` half is `chartLocus` membership (`w4-datb` §1.2's target), while the
94	`h⁰ = 1` half is what DAT-C's normalization and the GAP-2 uniqueness of the effective
95	representative consume.
96	
97	**The `S`-becomes-the-chart-index sentence that stood here is RETRACTED** (issue I-0615, and this
98	was its last residual site — the file header at the top of this module already carried the
99	correction, and the worksheet's `w4-datb` §1.2 SECOND AMENDMENT retracts it harder).  Coverage does
100	not feed `S` back as the chart index, because it does not need the drop at all:
101	`IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` and for **neither** effectivity **nor** degree `g`
102	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`, `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`).  What the drop's output
103	*is* needed for is DAT-C's canonical section and GAP-2's uniqueness, which do require `0 ≤ W` and
104	`h⁰ = 1` — i.e. the chart map's injectivity, not its coverage. -/
105	theorem exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
106	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
108	    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
109	    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
110	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
111	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
112	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
113	    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
114	    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
115	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
116	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
117	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
118	    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
119	    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
120	      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
121	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
122	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
123	    IsSplitWitness C (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K))
124	      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
125	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
126	        (∀ (x : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
127	          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)),
128	          coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
129	        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
130	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
131	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
132	  refine ⟨isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1, ?_⟩
133	  -- the χ-value at the fibre field, transported from `k` (genus is base-field invariant)
134	  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
135	  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so `chi_relCurve_baseField`'s
136	  -- `relCurve`-spelled binders do not synthesise without these three re-keyings.
137	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
138	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
139	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
140	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
141	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
142	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
143	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
144	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
145	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
146	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
147	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
148	  exact exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (K := L) g hχL P hdense hPcl hPdeg W₀ e hdeg h1
149	
150	end
151	
152	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2
8	
9	/-!
10	# B-5 step 3: `b = n` IS FORCED, AND IT IS THE CALIBRATION, NOT A DEFECT (I-0660 adjudicated)
11	
12	A reviewer (I-0660) measured that `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
13	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean:134`) has a hypothesis pack that **forces `b = g`**, and
14	concluded that its `hb` "cannot be DAT-0a's threshold" and that step 3 is therefore not
15	"derived".  **The arithmetic is right; the conclusion is one step too strong, and this file
16	settles which parts stand.**
17	
18	## What is confirmed, and it is a real correction to this lane's prose
19	
20	`ledger_forces_b_eq_n` reproduces the reviewer's derivation and generalises it: at a chart index
21	legal at parameter `n` — i.e. satisfying the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n` that
22	`chartValueTrans` / `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:382`) require — the
23	hypothesis `hdeg` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` **determines `b`**, and `b = n`.  So
24	`b` is *not* a free parameter that DAT-0a may instantiate: the chart index pins it.
25	
26	`hb_forces_h0_eq_one` then shows what `hb` at `b = n` amounts to on a genus-`g` curve at `n = g`:
27	**every** degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`.  That is false on any curve with a degree-`g`
28	effective divisor moving in a positive-dimensional family, and it is strictly stronger than
29	every threshold theorem in the tree (DAT-0a's bound is `n₁·deg F + 1 − χ = n₁·deg F + g` with
30	`0 < deg F`, so it exceeds `g` as soon as `n₁ ≥ 1`).  The reviewer's reading of the *strength*
31	is therefore confirmed, and sharpened: it is not merely "stronger than a threshold result", it
32	is a statement the χ-ledger converts into an `h⁰` equality for every divisor at once.
33	
34	## What does NOT follow — and this is the correction to the reviewer
35	
36	The reviewer's conclusion assumes `n = g`.  **`n` is a free parameter of the entire chart
37	layer.**  `divFunctor C π n`, `chartValue C π n m Z`, `chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg` and
38	`abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg` are all stated for an arbitrary `n : ℕ`; nothing in
39	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` or `DivSchemeAbel.lean` pins it.  `n = g` is where the *divisor
40	representability lane* instantiates (`divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause`,
41	`DivRepAffPullClause.lean:475`), and where `Pic^0` has the right dimension — but the coverage
42	theorem does not know that.
43	
44	So `b = n` is a **calibration equation between two independently chosen numbers**, and reading
45	it as "an over-constraint" versus "the definition of the chart parameter" depends entirely on
46	which of `n` and `b` is free.  `index_of_threshold` records the direction that is actually
47	available: given DAT-0a's threshold `b ≥ 0` at the splitting field, a chart index constraint at
48	parameter `b.toNat` makes `hdeg` hold **by construction**.  There is no obstruction to
49	satisfying `hdeg`; the obstruction is that satisfying it *at n = g* requires the sharp
50	vanishing.
51	
52	## THE HONEST STATUS OF STEP 3, therefore
53	
54	Three statements, all now machine-checked, none of which was the one the roadmap carried:
55	
56	1. `hdeg` is satisfiable, for every threshold `b ≥ 0`, at the chart parameter `n := b.toNat`
57	   (`index_of_threshold`).  So coverage-at-a-chart-index is not blocked.
58	2. At the *representability* parameter `n = g`, `hdeg` forces `b = g`, and `hb` at `b = g` is
59	   the sharp vanishing — **not available, and not expected to be true**
60	   (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`).
61	3. Hence the residue is neither "instantiate DAT-0a" (the roadmap's claim, too optimistic) nor
62	   "restate with slack" (the reviewer's repair, which as they themselves note runs into the
63	   `0 ≤ Σ` legality of the index).  It is: **reconcile the chart parameter with the threshold.**
64	   The chart family the atlas glues may be indexed by `m`, and `d₁ = classDeg k Θ > 0`, so the
65	   available move is to let the chart index *at parameter g* carry the slack in `Z` rather than
66	   in `n` — which is exactly `classDeg_presenting_twist_eq_add`'s `g + e` shape, whose own
67	   legality (`0 ≤ Σ`) is the open question.
68	
69	That is a genuinely different residue from the one the roadmap and the reviewer each named, and
70	it is recorded here rather than in prose only.
71	
72	## Main declarations
73	
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ledger_forces_b_eq_n` — the reviewer's derivation, at general `n`.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.index_of_threshold` — the converse: every nonneg threshold is realised as
76	  the ledger value of a legal index at parameter `b.toNat`.
77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.hb_forces_h0_eq_one` — what `hb` at `b = n` costs: on a curve with
78	  `χ = 1 − n`, every degree-`n` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`.
79	-/
80

82	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
83	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

85	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

87	universe u
88	
89	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
90	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
91	
92	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
93	
94	open AlgebraicJacobian
95	
96	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
97	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
98	
99	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
100	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
101	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
102	
103	noncomputable section
104	
105	/-! ## The reviewer's derivation, at a general chart parameter -/
106	
107	variable (C) in
108	/-- **THE CHART INDEX DETERMINES THE THRESHOLD** (I-0660, confirmed and generalised).
109	
110	At a chart index legal at parameter `n` — the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n` that
111	`chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` requires for the chart value to land in `pic^0` — the hypothesis
112	`hdeg` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` is *not* a way of feeding in a threshold: it
113	**forces** `b = n`.
114	
115	The reviewer stated this at `n = g` and read it as a defect.  Read at general `n` it is a
116	calibration: `b` and `n` are two independently chosen naturals and the ledger equates them.
117	Which one is "over-constrained" depends on which is free — see `index_of_threshold` for the
118	other direction, and the module docstring for why `n = g` is the case where this bites. -/
119	theorem ledger_forces_b_eq_n {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
120	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
121	    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
122	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
123	    (M₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
124	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
125	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
126	    (m n : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
127	    (hZ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
128	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
129	    (b : ℤ)
130	    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map
131	      ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
132	    b = (n : ℤ) := by
133	  rw [classDeg_presenting_twist C lam t hlam L M₀ hM₀ m Z, hZ] at hdeg
134	  omega
135	
136	variable (C) in
137	/-- **The converse direction: every nonnegative threshold is realised.**
138	
139	Given a threshold `b ≥ 0` and a legal chart index at parameter `b.toNat`, the `hdeg` of
140	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` holds **by construction**.  So `hdeg` is not an
141	unsatisfiable hypothesis and coverage-at-a-chart-index is not blocked by it — which is the half
142	of the reviewer's report that needs correcting.
143	
144	What this does *not* do is put the index at the representability parameter `n = g`.  That is the
145	whole remaining question, and `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` says what it would cost to answer it by
146	taking `b = g`. -/
147	theorem index_of_threshold {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
148	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
149	    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
150	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
151	    (M₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
152	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
153	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
154	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (b : ℤ) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b)
155	    (hZ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
156	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - b) :
157	    classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map
158	        ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
159	      = ((b.toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
160	  rw [classDeg_presenting_twist C lam t hlam L M₀ hM₀ m Z, hZ, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb0]
161	  ring
162	
163	/-! ## What the threshold hypothesis costs at `b = n` -/
164	
165	/-- **`hb` at `b = n` is the SHARP vanishing, and the χ-ledger turns it into an `h⁰` equality.**
166	
167	If every divisor of degree `≥ n` on the base-changed curve has `H¹ = 0`, then on a curve with
168	`χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` **every** divisor of degree exactly `n` has `h⁰ = 1`.
169	
170	This is the sharpened form of the reviewer's strength observation.  Their version — "strictly
171	stronger than any threshold result" — is a comparison with what the tree has; this is a
172	comparison with what is *true*: for `n = g ≥ 1` a degree-`g` divisor may well have `h⁰ ≥ 2` (any
173	`g`-tuple of points imposing dependent conditions), so `hb` at `b = g` is not merely unproved,
174	it is **false in general**.  Hence there is no route to B-5 that instantiates DAT-0a at `b = g`,
175	and the residue is the chart-parameter reconciliation described in the module docstring.
176	
177	One line from the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`
178	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) — recorded because the whole argument fits in it and the
179	conclusion is worth having in Lean rather than in a review comment. -/
180	theorem hb_forces_h0_eq_one
181	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
182	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
183	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
184	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
185	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
186	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
187	    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
188	    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
189	      (n : ℤ) ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
190	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
191	    (D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
192	    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D = (n : ℤ)) :
193	    (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) : ℤ) = 1 := by
194	  have h1 := hb D (le_of_eq hD.symm)
195	  have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) D h1
196	  rw [hD, hχ] at hanchor
197	  omega
198	
199	end
200	
201	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	
9	/-!
10	# DAT-B B-1 — the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop to `h⁰ = 1`
11	
12	The coverage-side normalization of the DAT-B worksheet (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage
14	argument), given an **admissible point oracle** `P` — a set of closed `K`-rational points
15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
17	
18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).
20	
21	The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5, worksheet §1.2 step 5) consumes this with
22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.
25	
26	## Route (worksheet §1.4, per step for the current `W'` with `h¹ = 0`, `deg = g + e'`)
27	
28	* **The bad locus is small** (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`): `H⁰(𝒪(W'))` is nonzero
29	  (rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`), its base divisor
30	  (`Scheme.baseDivisor`, the DD-F kit) has finite support consisting of closed points, so
31	  the non-base locus contains a nonempty open (complement of a finite closed set in the
32	  irreducible curve — it contains the generic point) and the oracle supplies an admissible
33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`
38	  (`Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt` through the `h⁰` bridge
39	  `finrank_divisorSections_top`) — while the χ-ledger (`chi_divisorSheaf`) with
40	  `residueDeg x = 1` and `h¹(𝒪(W')) = 0` gives `χ(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1`; equality

78	/-- **An admissible non-base point** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 1): if `H⁰(𝒪(W))` is nonzero
79	and `P` is dense (meets every nonempty open) and consists of closed points, then some
80	`x ∈ P` is *not* a base point of the system: some nonzero section `f ∈ H⁰(𝒪(W))` has
81	exact order at `x`, `(W + div f)ₓ = 0`.  The base locus is contained in the support of
82	the base divisor `bd(H⁰(𝒪(W)))` — a finite set of closed points, whose complement is a
83	nonempty open (it contains the generic point); the base-divisor achiever
84	(`Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
85	outside the support. -/
86	theorem exists_admissible_nonbase_point (P : Set Y)
87	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
88	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
89	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W)) :
90	    ∃ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (_ : x ∈ P) (f : Y.functionField)
91	      (_ : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0),
92	      coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
93	        = 0 := by
94	  classical
95	  set T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K W ⊤ with hT
96	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 := by
97	    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
98	    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=
99	      finrank_divisorSections_top K W
100	    rw [hbot, finrank_bot] at hfr
101	    omega
102	  set B : Y.CurveDivisor := Scheme.baseDivisor K T W hTne with hB
103	  -- the support of the base divisor is a finite set of closed points
104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=
105	    isClosed_biUnion_finset (fun p _ =>
106	      isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2)
107	  set U : Y.Opens :=
108	    ⟨(⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y))ᶜ, hclosed.isOpen_compl⟩ with hU
109	  have hUne : (U : Set Y).Nonempty := by
110	    refine ⟨genericPoint Y, fun hmem => ?_⟩
111	    obtain ⟨p, _, hp⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp hmem
112	    exact p.2 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hp).symm
113	  obtain ⟨x, hxP, hxU⟩ := hdense U hUne
114	  have hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y := hPcl x hxP
115	  -- outside the support the base multiplicity vanishes
116	  have hxc : x ∉ ⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y) := hxU
117	  have hxB : coeffAt hx B = 0 := by
118	    by_contra hne
119	    exact hxc (Set.mem_iUnion₂.mpr
120	      ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hne, rfl⟩)
121	  have hBat : (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T W ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) = 0 := by
122	    rw [← Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hTne hx]
123	    exact hxB
124	  -- the achiever realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
125	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, hach⟩ :=
126	    Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K (le_refl T) hTne hx
127	  exact ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfT, hf, hach.trans hBat⟩
